purpose: Machine-readable evidence for the HAL experiment blog. This file stores gameplay means, direct treatment deltas, setup differences, and source breadcrumbs.

metrics.stock: net stocks per active game minute; higher is better
metrics.damage: net damage per active game minute; higher is better

uncertainty_policy.rule: Form the treatment-minus-control difference first. Use paired match or boot differences when both arms share evaluation units. Otherwise combine independent standard errors.
uncertainty_policy.warning: Do not subtract arm-level lower confidence bounds. A saved one-sided lower bound is not a confidence interval for the treatment difference.
uncertainty_policy.missing: Most historical runs retain only aggregate means and one-sided lower bounds. Their direct difference interval is null until match_rows.json is consolidated.
uncertainty_policy.reported_head_intervals: The O43 architecture table contains direct treatment-minus-control 95% intervals supplied with the completed ablation. Other entries do not claim a direct interval unless stated.

evidence_levels.strong: One planned factor changes. Model size, data, training work, and evaluation are otherwise matched, or the same checkpoint is evaluated twice.
evidence_levels.strong_rejection: The treatment had more model capacity, data, or work and still lost. This is strong evidence against the tested treatment package, although the resource mismatch prevents an exact effect-size estimate.
evidence_levels.near: The comparison is useful, but one secondary input also changes.
evidence_levels.package: Several factors change. The result tests the complete package only.
evidence_levels.descriptive: No causal treatment comparison is available.
evidence_levels.missing: The run was not completed or a suitable control does not exist.

studies.title: Legacy controller classes versus Cartesian controller classes
studies.setup: 15.05M parameters; batch 512; 16,384 updates; 8.39M examples; ranked-anonymized-1 v7; O26 loss; matched H4 evaluation.

comparison.uncertainty_note: Direct match-level interval not yet consolidated.

studies.claim: The legacy codec did not explain the old performance. In this bridge it was worse.

studies.title: Cartesian stick classes versus fixed polar stick classes
studies.setup: 14.48M proxy; batch 512; 16,384 updates; 2^30 supervised positions; ranked-anonymized-1 v8; all AdamW; D2/R2; same 96 matchups.

comparison.uncertainty_note: The matchups are shared, but the paired match rows have not been consolidated here.

studies.claim: The fixed polar grid gave a small stock gain and almost no damage gain.

studies.title: Projectile inputs
studies.setup: 7.1M policy; batch 128; 16,384 updates; 2.10M examples; ranked-anonymized-1 v7; four pooled projectile slots.
studies.claim: Projectile state gave a small positive effect.

studies.title: Ice Climbers follower inputs
studies.setup: The observation token has four player blocks: ego, ego follower, opponent follower, opponent. Missing follower values use masks.
studies.claim: The feature path is known, but no clean gameplay ablation was found.

studies.title: Past-action input encoding
studies.setup: O26 family; context 128; 15.05M versus 15.22M parameters. The one-hot arm used batch 1,024 and saw 16.78M examples; the learned physical encoding used batch 512 and saw 8.39M.

comparison.uncertainty_note: The one-hot arm had more parameters and twice the data and still lost. The direction is persuasive; the mismatch prevents a precise causal effect size.

studies.claim: A learned class embedding plus physical stick and trigger values is better than one-hot action history.

studies.title: Rare one-hot button classes
studies.setup: Same O28 family; batch 1,024; 16,384 updates; 16.78M examples.
studies.claim: Pruning rare one-hot classes did not give a clear overall gain.

studies.title: Hand-designed spatial features
studies.setup: Derived relative position, velocity, range, and stage geometry were appended to the frame token.
studies.claim: Both attempts stopped before a valid closed-loop result. Do not call this a negative result.

studies.title: Lean observation feature bundle
studies.setup: d256, 8 layers, context 256, batch 512, 16,384 updates, 8.39M examples; old evaluation protocol.
studies.claim: Removing or changing the state-feature bundle hurt play. The test does not identify one responsible column.

studies.title: Run-length and BPE action spans
studies.setup: d256, 8 layers, context 256, batch 512, 16,384 updates, 8.39M examples; variable spans up to 16 frames; 7.75M parameters.

comparison.uncertainty_note: Output representation, execution cadence, parameters, and crash rate changed.

studies.claim: The complete tested RLE/BPE policy failed. This does not isolate compression itself.

studies.title: One joint controller token per frame
studies.setup: The main stick, C-stick, two triggers, and buttons were packed into one data-derived chord class.
studies.claim: The retained run stopped after three diagnostic updates. There is no gameplay result.

studies.title: Across-frame and within-frame action feedback
studies.setup: 7.148M parameters in every arm; batch 512; 16,384 updates; 8.39M examples; ranked-anonymized-1 v7; same H4 96-boot protocol.

arms.name: D0: no across-frame feedback; no learned within-frame feedback

studies.claim: Both types of feedback helped at H4. Across-frame feedback had the larger average effect.

studies.title: Next-frame, independent multi-frame, and autoregressive multi-frame prediction
studies.setup: Representative runs: next-frame vlim96s9; independent multi-frame shjnxxsu; autoregressive multi-frame 5wfk2esf or tgpuo1be.
studies.claim: Use this as design history. O37 isolates action feedback; the older lineage does not form a clean score ladder.

studies.title: Order of controller parts within one frame
studies.setup: The current order is C-stick, main stick, triggers, buttons.
studies.claim: No clean order ablation was found. O37 tests feedback versus no learned feedback, not alternate orders.

studies.title: FiLM initialization, action-head shape, and trunk-to-logit skip
studies.setup: O43 arm A control; 15.05M class; batch 512; ranked-anonymized-1; same initialization and evaluation units. Each arm changes one component.

arms.name: replace SiLU MLP heads with normalized linear heads

control.name: ordinary FiLM initialization; SiLU MLP heads; trunk-to-logit skip

studies.claim: Each O42-like removal hurt in its O43 test. The 4,096-update FiLM result can also reflect slower learning, so it does not prove the final-step result.

studies.title: FiLM versus plain feature concatenation
studies.setup: O37 compares active FiLM with the same FiLM layers fed fixed zero inputs. O43 tests FiLM initialization. Neither test uses plain concatenation as the treatment.
studies.claim: There is no FiLM-versus-concatenation ablation.

studies.title: O26 to O42 architecture and sampler package
studies.setup: Equal-step comparison. O42 uses SwiGLU trunk and temporal blocks, normalized linear action heads, no trunk-to-logit skip, zero-initialized bounded FiLM, normalized temporal input, symmetric residual scaling, and a different one-window sampler.
studies.claim: The complete O42 package was worse. Its many simultaneous changes prevent a component claim.

studies.title: Historical action-head capacity test
studies.setup: Historical O23 comparison. The larger state MLP used 12.6% more parameters and compute.
studies.claim: This suggested a small gain, but the later O43 one-change test is much stronger evidence for nonlinear heads.

studies.title: Training-only future-state expert
studies.setup: O26 actor plus a future-state auxiliary model; 16.31M total parameters; batch 1,024; 16.78M examples; more than twice the estimated training work.
studies.claim: The tested auxiliary expert did not help despite favorable resource differences.

studies.title: Output queries cross-attend to trunk history
studies.setup: O24 used 20 action-prefix queries with causal cross-attention over prior trunk tokens.
studies.claim: The nearest reference also changes the trunk, codec, offsets, and decoder size. Keep the arm score, but do not report a causal delta.

studies.title: Controller parts flattened into the main Transformer sequence
studies.setup: Each frame became one state token plus four controller-part tokens, so a 256-frame context became 1,280 tokens and used about five times the trunk work.
studies.claim: Both arms are interesting historical systems, but neither has a clean equal-work control.

studies.title: Fixed twelve-frame prediction delay
studies.setup: O43 delay 1 versus O44 delay 12. O44 kept H6/R1 but used a longer future-data buffer.
studies.claim: The long-delay package failed. The buffer difference prevents a delay-only effect estimate.

studies.title: Rank-weighted behavior cloning
studies.setup: Exact O26 policy and training recipe; Platinum, Diamond, and Master replay weights 1, 2, and 4; batch 512; 16,384 updates; 8.39M examples.
studies.claim: Replay-rank weighting did not help. This is not advantage-weighted regression.

studies.title: Detached-value advantage-weighted regression
studies.setup: 7.15M O37-style actor; batch 512; 16,384 updates; 8.39M examples; ranked-anonymized-1 v7. BC used 96 boots and AWR used 128 boots, so the evaluations are not paired.
studies.claim: AWR gave a modest, consistent gain in the modern comparison.

studies.title: AWR return horizon
studies.setup: 14.48M O52 proxy; batch 512; 16,384 updates; 2^30 supervised positions; ranked-anonymized-1 v8; D2/R2; 96 boots. Gamma is the planned treatment.
studies.claim: AWR improved when the return half-life was long enough to reach the actions that caused later rewards. The middle setting was best in this three-point sweep.

studies.title: Sparse endpoint flow
studies.setup: Same d256 trunk, data, updates, examples, H4, and 96-boot protocol as O37 D3. Flow used 8.95M parameters, 25.2% more training work, four flow steps, and 7.3% more estimated inference work.
studies.claim: The tested flow package was worse despite more capacity and work.

studies.title: Continuous controller flow prototype
studies.setup: 4.994M parameters; d256, 6 layers, 8 heads; 256 context frames plus 16 action queries; eight flow steps; effective batch 512; 131,072 updates; 67.11M examples; old evaluation protocol.
studies.claim: This early model generated continuous stick and trigger values, but it has no matched control. Architecture, loss, action format, training budget, and execution all differ from the later policies.

studies.title: Attached implicit Q-learning
studies.setup: Exact O26 policy path plus Q and value heads; batch 1,024; 16,384 updates; 16.78M examples; 1.43% more total parameters; about twice the estimated training work.
studies.claim: The tested IQL system failed despite more data, capacity, and work. This does not reject all offline Q-learning methods.

studies.title: Exploration Modeling with one or eight latent trajectories
studies.setup: O26 trunk with a non-causal parallel trajectory decoder. K=1 used batch 1,024, 16,384 updates, and 16.78M examples. K=8 stopped at 10,240 updates and changed microbatching.

comparisons.uncertainty_note: K=8 used much more trajectory compute per example but stopped earlier, so K is not isolated.

studies.claim: K=8 was much better than K=1, but neither tested XM system beat O26 behavior cloning.

studies.title: One training window per replay
studies.setup: Same d256 independent multi-frame model; batch 1,024; 16,384 updates; 16.78M examples; old evaluation protocol. Only the recorded windows-per-replay setting changed.
studies.claim: One window per replay improved stock score, while damage score fell slightly. The current replay ring should repeat this test before treating it as universal.

studies.title: Policy-world v8 data cleaning
studies.setup: v8 keeps human games where both players dealt more than 50 damage and both started with four stocks.
studies.claim: v8 removed 0.405% of training replays and 0.198% of training frames. No clean gameplay test isolates this cleaning.

studies.title: Ranked-only data versus all 44 sources
studies.setup: O42 architecture. The corrected comparison uses equal update counts; ranked-anonymized-1 is the control and the natural 44-source mix is the treatment.
studies.claim: The full mix improved damage but did not improve stock at equal training steps.

studies.title: Real-time chunking with queued-action feedback
studies.setup: The treatment trained dense offsets 1 through 20 with random committed prefixes. The only retained treatment run, c6yd7zxx, stopped at 4,096 updates. The planned dense autoregressive control was not run.
studies.claim: RTC is unresolved. The treatment score alone does not show whether queued-action feedback helped.

studies.title: Frames executed before replanning
studies.setup: Each of four fixed checkpoints was evaluated at 1, 2, 4, and 6 frames per plan. In this older runtime, execution horizon and replan interval are the same setting.
studies.claim: Longer execution hurt the models that did not receive across-frame feedback. It had little effect on D3. This is not a replan-only test.

studies.title: Half of the action loss on the next frame
studies.setup: Same legacy codec and O43 architecture; batch 512; 16,384 updates; ranked-anonymized-1. The bridge changes only loss allocation.
studies.claim: More weight on the next frame recovered part of the legacy-codec penalty.

studies.title: Additional far-future target
studies.setup: Historical near-control. Adding offset 18 also reduced the relative share of offset 1.
studies.claim: The extra far target did not help, but target distance and next-frame loss share changed together.

studies.title: Batch size at fixed examples
studies.setup: Every arm saw 2.097M examples. Smaller batches therefore received more optimizer updates.
studies.claim: At fixed examples, more optimizer updates helped. This is a batch-and-update trade, not batch size alone.

studies.title: Muon and AdamW learning-rate pair
studies.setup: Fixed model and data. Muon and AdamW rates moved together.
studies.claim: The best point was inside the sweep. The test selects a rate pair, not one optimizer's rate alone.

studies.title: Ego-player identity conditioning
studies.setup: 16M model; 16,384 updates; Fox-only model side; 96 boots. The baseline uses the same trained model and evaluation but masks the player embedding.
studies.claim: Identity changes behavior. Cody raised damage strongly, but not every identity improved stock.

studies.title: Muon plus AdamW versus all AdamW
studies.setup: 216.5M production architecture; 131,072 updates; full policy-world-v8 corpus; 96-boot standard evaluation. The optimizer recipe, including rates and parameter routing, is the treatment.

arms.name: Muon matrices plus AdamW other parameters

studies.claim: The all-AdamW production recipe won. This is an optimizer-recipe result, not a pure algorithm result.

studies.title: Offline loss and gameplay across training
studies.setup: 216.5M Muon production run; full policy-world-v8; 96 boots at each completed checkpoint.
studies.claim: Validation likelihood improved steadily, but gameplay was not monotonic. Checkpoint selection needs closed-loop evaluation.

studies.title: Model size, data, and control timing
studies.setup: The older O39 sweep shows strong interactions between size and deployment timing. O54 is the replacement measurement and is still outside this frozen evidence set.
studies.claim: Do not publish one monotonic size claim from the older sweep. Use the new matched size and latency results when complete.
